Paternity index

Source: R/frns2.R
patidx.Rd

The weight of the DNA evidence that an alleged father is the father of a child, against an unrelated man, locus by locus and overall. With the mother's genotype the index uses the allele the child must have received from the father; without it the index is the parent-child kinidx(). There is no allowance for mutation, so one inconsistent locus gives an index of 0. See proof("patidx").

Usage

patidx(child, father, freq, mother = NULL)

Arguments

child, father

Genotypes: two-column matrices of allele labels, one row per locus, or two alleles for one locus.

freq

The population frequencies of the child's alleles, same shape.

mother

NULL, or the mother's genotype in the same form.

Value

A list: locus, a data frame with locus and idx (NaN where the mother's genotype rules her out as mother); log10idx; and post, the probability of paternity at even prior odds.

Examples

patidx(child = c(12, 14), father = c(14, 15), freq = c(0.1, 0.2),
       mother = c(12, 12))
#> $locus
#>   locus idx
#> 1     1 2.5
#> 
#> $log10idx
#> [1] 0.39794
#> 
#> $post
#> [1] 0.7142857
#>
